html:
SMTO-TSK-0023 — SMTO can't find this task

GUID: 8fdb3bd0-ac81-465e-bc13-2b661f857fa3
Slug: task-not-found
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The task this action points to isn't part of this conversation anymore. It may have been deleted, or the page is pointing at a task from another conversation. Nothing was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page, then open the conversation from the Conversations pane. The page may still show a task that was deleted or that belongs to another conversation.
  2. Use the buttons on a task that appears in this conversation now, usually the latest reply. SMTO only acts on tasks that belong to the conversation you are viewing.
  3. If the task is gone, send a new message asking for the work you still need. A deleted task can't be brought back by repeating the old action, but a new task can do the work.

What success looks like

  • The action works on a task shown in the conversation, or your new task starts.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If the missing task was changing files or other systems, check what it already did before asking for the work again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested task or run is missing, removed, belongs to a different conversation, or is not the kind of chat task the control expects.

What this means

  • The task/run record is missing, tombstoned, belongs to another conversation or is not the chat-task type expected by the control. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The task/run record is missing, tombstoned, belongs to another conversation or is not the chat-task type expected by the control.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh the owning task list and check task type, conversation identity and retention state.

How to fix it

  • Check the request_id and conversation_id in Technical details: the task must exist, not be tombstoned, belong to that conversation and be a chat task. Reload the conversation's task list and act on a retained task it owns; a removed task cannot be recreated by resubmitting its old request identity.
  • Refresh the conversation’s task list and select a retained task owned by that conversation. A removed historical task cannot be recreated by resubmitting its old execution identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected retained task belongs to the intended conversation and supports the action.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
